title: Russia May Launch Nuclear Weapon Into Orbit As Soon As Next Month
description:
Western intelligence agencies reportedly believe Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit as early as December, "suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought," reports Ars Technica, citing German media reports. Such a launch would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, while a detonation could create radiation belts that damage satellites for years. From the report: The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.
 
Reporting from three German news outlets -- public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Munich-based newspaper Suddeutsche Zeitung -- indicates Russia's launch of a nuclear-armed satellite could be imminent. The report says Western intelligence agencies, including the German Armed Forces and Federal Intelligence Service, believe Russia is preparing to deploy the weapon in space this year. Several NATO countries have exchanged their findings on the matter.
 
The nuclear-armed satellite, designated Sputnik-S, has been in storage in the greater Moscow area for years, the German news report said. German Space Command believes the satellite could be launched as early as December. Once in orbit, a nuclear weapon could loiter for months or years, ready for detonation on the command of Russian military forces. The Kremlin dismissed the report. "Given the number of qualifiers like 'allegedly' and 'possibly' -- not to mention the fact that the claims are attributed to some unspecified source -- they are hardly worth taking seriously," said Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Russian President Vladimir Putin.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: New York Bans Subscription and Post-Purchase Fees On Cars
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from WGNA-FM: On November 23rd, New York State Governor Kathy Hochul announced Bill S.9348A/A.10411A. This bill aims to put money back in New Yorkers pockets by prohibiting any vehicle manufacturers, dealers, or third-party providers from charging consumers more money for locked services or subscription fees. This specifically targets newer vehicles that may lock pre-installed features (like heated seats or screen compatibility) behind a paywall or subscription service. This is becoming more and more of a problem as years go by, and consumers have been very vocal against the practice, but this is a tangible step that can be taken to end this practice before it gets too out of hand. [...] The bill will go into effect on February 27th, 2027. "No one should have to pay recurring fees just to use features in a car they already bought. My office has secured millions of dollars for New Yorkers throughout the state who were charged illegal junk fees when purchasing a car," said New York Attorney General Letitia James stated. "Unfair fees are fueling rising costs, and I am proud to work with Governor Hochul and the legislature to bring costs down."

title: Google Is Finally Retiring the Nest App Early Next Year
description:
Google is shutting down its 15-year-old Nest app on January 25, 2027, requiring users to switch to Google Home to remotely control their smart home devices and receive notifications. "Then, on August 2, the company will retire Google Assistant on smart speakers and displays, with Gemini replacing the older tech for voice controls," reports Engadget. From the report: If you've yet to migrate your Nest devices to the Google Home app, the company says your existing settings and schedules will transfer over automatically. The only thing you need to manually move over are any custom clips you might have saved over the years. You can do this by visiting the Nest website before January 25 and clicking the "Download all" button. Google says it will automatically migrate Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions to its newer Google Home Premium package. "You will receive an email closer to the date of transfer detailing your subscription information," the company adds. "The Nest app launched over 15 years ago, and home technology has changed a lot since then," Google says of the decision. "To give every Nest user Google's latest security protections and most advanced cyber defenses, plus new features from Gemini, we're bringing all Nest devices together in the Google Home app."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Trump Halts Army's Plans to Detonate Bomb-Making Chemicals In Iowa
description:
President Trump has ordered the military to halt plans to detonate nearly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. "Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January," reports Ars Technica. From the report: The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).
 
Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.
 
Late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice's request to put a hold on the Army's permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and plans.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: CrowdStrike to Buy Zscaler In $44 Billion Deal
description:
CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire network security provider Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal. "The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks," reports CNBC. The acquisition is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028. From the report: "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen."
 
CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind market leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.
 
[...] Analysts view the Zscaler deal as a major AI security opportunity, allowing CrowdStrike to capture more customer security spending and close a significant gap with Palo Alto. "The addition of ZS to CRWD's platform could bring more breadth in an era of vendor consolidation and, more importantly, network security to position the company more effectively for rising demand for AI Sovereignty," wrote analysts at JPMorgan.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Trump Is Said to Have Directed Effort to Reinstate Nvidia Chief
description:
President Trump reportedly directed a behind-the-scenes effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, enlisting Vice President JD Vance to secure assurances from federal officials that Huang was not facing criminal charges or considered a national security risk. According to The New York Times, the intervention came despite intelligence concerns surrounding Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy linked to an investigation into illegal Nvidia chip shipments to China. From the report: [...] Only a tiny handful of officials at the highest level of the government were aware of these conversations. On Sunday night, Nvidia's board told the administration that it would be announcing Mr. Huang's reinstatement on Monday morning before the markets opened. The announcement included a note about a new compliance committee, intended to offer public assurance that the company was taking seriously the investigation into the possible smuggling of advanced chips. Mr. Trump was said to have been thrilled that the plan to restore Mr. Huang was executed without any leaks.
 
In directing Mr. Vance to engage with Mr. Huang and his peers, Mr. Trump was turning to one of the members of his administration with the strongest relationships in Silicon Valley. The vice president is close to some of Mr. Huang's biggest supporters and admirers, such as David Sacks, the investor and co-chairman of the President's Council of Advisers on Science and Technology. Mr. Sacks previously served as Mr. Trump's key adviser on artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency issues.
 
On Monday morning, Mr. Trump rejoiced in Nvidia's action, saying on his social media website Truth Social that the company "made the correct and proper decision." The president explicitly connected the reinstatement of Mr. Huang to the health of the U.S. economy. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Mr. Trump wrote.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: YC Startup Working On 'Cost Per Kill' For Missiles
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Wired: At 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. But he's not too young to win half a million dollars for his AI-guided-missile startup. In September, Dandzbergs, who was born in Latvia, was admitted to Y Combinator's fall 2026 cohort. The startup accelerator counts companies like Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, and Reddit among its alumni; Dandzbergs is likely the youngest solo founder in its vaunted history. His startup, Polemos Industries, is attempting to develop a new class of precision-guided missile that can be easily and cheaply manufactured, can be fired from portable launchers, and can resist jamming attempts. "I think missiles are the coolest thing," Dandzbergs tells WIRED. "A lot of people that have found success in engineering early on have had a passion for blowing stuff up."
 
In conversation, Dandzbergs is poised and articulate. He talks about "attacking hard problems," breaking things down to "first principles," and how the Ukraine conflict has forever altered the theater of war -- a personal fixation, given his country's proximity to Russia. He projects an unassailable confidence in his own abilities. "He's a pretty exceptional person," says Harj Taggar, a YC partner assigned to mentor Dandzbergs. "I'm still somewhat in disbelief that we're talking about a 16-year-old." Dandzbergs has resolved to apply these unusual talents to figuring out how to optimize targeted killing. His startup's guiding ambition, according to its investor one-pager, is to bring down the "cost per kill." Dandzbergs hopes to demonstrate a prototype missile by December. Despite concerns about the ethical implications of autonomous weapons and his young age, he remains undeterred. "I want to be part of it. I want to move with the future of warfare," he says.
 
"Please don't say I'm sacrificing my childhood," says Dandzbergs. "This is the childhood I dreamed of."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: US Intelligence Chief Predicts More Tech Outages As Systems Undergo Upgrades
description:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Sunday that Americans should expect more technology outages as companies and government agencies modernize aging infrastructure. Speaking on CNN, Clayton said the upgrades are necessary to improve performance and cybersecurity but will inevitably cause "glitches, gaps, [and] interruptions in service." Reuters reports: A string of technology failures this month disrupted critical U.S. systems, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft outage that hit email services, a technical glitch that affected several major banks, and a temporary disruption to the National Security Agency's network.
 
Speaking on the ABC program "This Week," Clayton reiterated his previous statements that those outages were not the result of coordinated or state-sponsored actions, attributing them to technical upgrades. Clayton declined to discuss specifics of separate reports of cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture, saying he expects investigators to provide answers "in due course." Clayton told CNN: "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road."
 
Microsoft President Brad Smith issued a similar warning on CBS News' Face the Nation: "I think we have to be prepared, frankly, for the coming months because this isn't the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks ... The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Anthropic's Safety-Conscious Corporate Culture Still Envisions Superintelligent AI
description:
The Washington Post looks at Anthropic's "unique" corporate culture, where CEO Dario Amodei "leads his workforce through essays, long memos posted in Slack and twice-monthly all-hands talks jokingly known as 'Dario Vision Quests'... 

"The CEO's output has established a constellation of beliefs treated as obvious, urgent and righteous inside the company: AI that supersedes humans is inevitable, the United States must limit China's AI development, and Claude might be conscious."

Inside this tight-knit culture, Anthropic staffers, who call themselves Ants, get to feel that they are working on the world's most urgent problems, with the smartest people, in a shared mission to safeguard humanity, according to interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with the company's ethos, including several current and former employees. At its core is a belief that Anthropic — and Amodei — know what's best for the world... "A pervasive thing at Anthropic is: We're going to put on our capes and we're going to be the responsible ones, and we're going to accrue great power, but ... because we're doing it responsibly, it's responsible to acquire more power," said a former employee who left the company this year and, like others, spoke on the condition of anonymity to avoid retaliation from the company.... 

Its message to investors fit with a vision of the future that Amodei often sketches out for his staff, people familiar with the company said, in which AI companies have the power of nation-states. After nearly six years of telling his workers that powerful AI will force society's leaders to makep difficult decisions, Amodei is now one of the powers who must decide how to act, in a major test of the corporate culture he has created.... [Amodei] set out to create a more safety-conscious culture when he co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six people from his inner circle, most of them from OpenAI. In an internal memo the following year, Amodei laid out the stakes. "The current trajectory of AI development makes me think that there's a 20 to 30 percent chance that AGI will lead to the destruction or permanent stunting of humanity," he wrote, referring to the concept of artificial general intelligence, previously unreported court records show. He added that truly capable AI "seems more powerful/dangerous than nuclear weapons." 

Amodei was careful about those he hired to work on that existential challenge. Recruits were screened with a "culture interview," even for back office and policy roles, according to former employees and an archived copy of the company's careers page... It's "a bit of an 'are you ready for the cult' interview," an Anthropic hiring manager texted the unsuccessful candidate, according to a screenshot reviewed by The Post... 

Before ringing in Anthropic's record initial public offering at Times Square in New York on Thursday, Amodei delivered a short speech with some of his greatest hits. "To state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control," Amodei said.






Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Alice Huang In Touch With Chinese Spy Agency During Affair With Nvidia CEO, NYT Says
description:
Reuters reports:


Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia's recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters... 

The scandal has also prompted a deeper look at Washington's approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the prized semiconductors.
 
Reuters points out that several U.S. officials "have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy..." 

"A spokesperson for Jensen Huang declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang for comment..." But the New York Times also reported U.S. intelligence agencies have gathered evidence "that Ms. Huang's business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency." 


American author/journalist Greg Palast has his own unconfirmed theory, speculating that maybe Alice Huang wasn't a romantic interest but the Nvidia CEO's "business conduit to the Chinese military industrial complex... arranging the secret handoff of roughly one in five Nvidia chips."

Why did the two Huang's make the affair so obvious? If she's a spy, why flaunt it before TV cameras and paparazzi? Because Huang and Huang wanted you to know... If Jensen and this guy's wife are conspiring to move hot chips to China, they can't exactly talk about it over the phone or in emails. So, they agree to meet-up in various hotel rooms during business conferences, doors locked...






Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: GrapheneOS Accuses Google of Kneecapping Its Android Partners Using Pixel Exclusives
description:
Last year Slashed reported that the privacy- and security-focused Android fork GrapheneOS was "partnering with a major Android OEM to bring its hardened, de-Googled OS to Snapdragon-powered flagship phones." 
 And early this November Motorola announced their upcoming high end Signature 27 phone would include official support for GrapheneOS as an OS option, the first Motorola device supporting GrapheneOS. 

But the nonprofit GrapheneOS project has a new problem, reports the blog It's FOSS :


GrapheneOS has accused Google of leaning on phone makers to keep away from the project. The claim came in a thread on X [Thursday], where the project says makers were questioned about working with it, then threatened over their Google app licensing.... The project says Google is working against GrapheneOS itself and expects it to go further. It sees Pixel bootloaders being locked down eventually and Play Integrity, an API it calls illegal, being pushed harder. And if that were to happen, Android forks would struggle to survive under that. 

GrapheneOS believes some of Google's conduct breaks US criminal law and that antitrust violations can put individuals in prison. It wants to talk to the [U.S.] Department of Justice and says earlier cases against Google left its most serious violations largely untouched. Supporters are being asked for introductions to prosecutors and regulators, with assurances that the project has the necessary resources to carry on no matter what happens. 

GrapheneOS says more Android features and updates now stay Pixel only, leaving other hardware partners behind.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: America's Shipping Ports Now Face Thousands of Cyberattacks Each Day
description:
"A number of ports across the U.S. are reporting an onslaught of cyberattacks," reports The Hill, "amid a growing number of AI-enabled attacks targeting notable infrastructure."


The Port of Corpus Christi, Texas, which functions as the U.S.'s largest passage of oil exports, said it was targeted with "hundreds if not thousands" of attacks per day, according to reporting from the Financial Times. The port's chief executive, Kent Britton, told the outlet that attacks surged from "known bad actor" countries and organizations that are searching for high-profile targets. ["Experts link countries like Iran, North Korea and China to hacking operations targeting shipping infrastructure," the Financial Times reports.] The attacks against Corpus Christi's port went after its computer systems by attempting to find weaknesses. Attackers also sent phishing messages, posing as senior executives, to trick staff into allowing them access, per the Financial Times... 

"They're poking at our systems and trying to find vulnerabilities," Britton said. "With AI, it'll only get more complicated." He stated the port was seeking additional help from Washington but "if you're playing defence, you have to get it right every time ... if you're planning offence, you only have to get it right once." 

The Port of Los Angeles — the country's busiest port — similarly stated that in August it had stopped 120 million attempted attacks into its networks through network exploitation, credential harvesting and malware attacks, Bloomberg reported. Gene Seroka, executive director of the Port of Los Angeles, expressed that all potential attackers "have to do is to get it right one time" and that it was "front of mind every day." 
"The attacks have escalated sharply in recent months..." reports the Financial Times, "exposing vulnerabilities in the ageing networks that enable international commerce."


The FBI last week warned that hackers are using an AI tool named Artex to automate cyber attacks... The threat is growing across the US. The US Coast Guard reported a 17% increase in cyber maritime incidents last year and investigated cyber attacks on two US-bound oil tankers in August with the FBI... The agencies said the joint offshore security boardings on August 21 and 24 were to "ensure integrity of the vessel's operational and information technology systems following indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised"... 

Ports are taking action to defend their waterways. The Port of Virginia, a major hub for consumer goods, agriculture and coal, said the threat of attacks is now "more acute because of the rise of AI". It is heavily investing in its cyber security team, with employees undergoing monthly training and drills with the US Coast Guard.... The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey is also investing heavily in cyber defence. A spokesperson said it has "multiple independent layers of protection" and "recovery plans with terminal operators and partners, so that critical operations can continue and cargo can keep moving". Other ports are reluctant to discuss the threat they face — and their defences. The Port of Oakland said it would not publicly discuss its "cyber security defences or protective measures", citing national security concerns. 

The article notes it's not just affecting U.S. ports. "Cybersecurity company Shieldworkz said Russia's Noname057(16) threatened European operators this October...





Read more of this story at Slashdot.
